page: Google Cloud Platform m4-ultramem-56 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for workloads demanding extensive in-memory footprints. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 56 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 1488 GB of system memory. This configuration achieves an exceptional memory-to-core ratio of approximately 26.57 GB per vCPU, placing it among the most memory-dense instances available in cloud infrastructure.

From an architectural perspective, the instance operates without integrated local storage and contains zero GPUs. Storage operations rely entirely on external network-attached volumes, allowing users to configure persistent block storage independently according to throughput and capacity requirements. Because local NVMe disks and specialized accelerators are omitted, resource investment is focused strictly on dedicated compute and massive random-access memory rather than unneeded auxiliary hardware.

This platform profile is primarily tailored for enterprise-scale memory-bound applications. Appropriate workload fits include large in-memory databases like SAP HANA, extensive Redis or Memcached caching tiers, in-memory data analytics engines, and enterprise resource planning platforms that require huge working sets retained directly in RAM.
